items.entity: Supports of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives only the sampling rule: 1–4 constraints, either fixed points at corners or edge midpoints, or 'fixed segments connecting these locations'. The number, positions and point/segment type for this instance appear only in Fig. 3; the caption states no boundary conditions. The text also does not say whether a 'segment' is a half edge (corner to midpoint) or a full edge (corner to corner).
readings: Entire left edge fixed (corner-to-corner segment, cantilever-like)
Half of left edge fixed (bottom-left corner to left-edge midpoint)
Bottom-left and bottom-right corner nodes fixed
Bottom-left corner node + right-edge midpoint node fixed
Multi-constraint case (up to 4), e.g. entire bottom edge + top-right corner node fixed

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says 'fixed points in the corners or midpoints of edges' but not whether a point support is one node (on the 65×65 node grid the midpoint node is index 32) or a small group of nodes. This changes the local stress concentration and the material layout near the support.
readings: Single node with u_x and u_y fixed

items.entity: Single external load of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance
items.description: Sec. 4.1 only says 'A single external load was applied along the edge of the domain'. Which edge, and where along it, appears only in Fig. 3. 'The edge' could mean one fixed edge or any edge. The units and origin of (x_load, y_load) in Eq. 25 are not defined.
readings: Right edge (x = L) at mid-height, y = 0.5L
Right edge at bottom-right corner node (y = 0)

items.entity: Single external load of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only 'direction sampled randomly'. The angle for this instance is shown only in the figure, and the sampling distribution (any angle or a fixed set of angles) is not stated. Only the angle modulo 180° matters, because reversing a single load leaves the compliance and the optimal layout unchanged.
readings: Other sampled angle, e.g. 30° or 60° from +x

items.description: Sec. 4.1 says the load is 'applied along the edge' with unit magnitude. It does not say whether this is a force at one node or a load spread over several nodes or part of an edge. The single load coordinate in Eq. 25 suggests a point load, but the text never says so.
readings: Unit force at a single boundary node
Unit total force spread over 3 adjacent boundary nodes
Uniform traction of total magnitude 1 along the whole loaded edge

items.entity: Target volume fraction f of the Fig. 3 row-1 instance
items.description: Sec. 4.1 says only that f is drawn from a uniform distribution between 0.3 and 0.5 for each sample. The value for this instance is not given in the text; at most it can be read from Fig. 3.

Neither Sec. 2 nor Sec. 4.1 mentions any filter (type or radius). SIMP on a 64×64 grid without a filter gives checkerboard, mesh-dependent designs, so the SIMP ground truth cannot be reproduced without knowing the filter.

Sec. 2 says the run stops when the relative compliance change falls below 'a specified tolerance' (no value given) or when a maximum iteration count is reached. Sec. 4.1 says '100 optimization steps as the stopping criterion' while also pointing to the Sec. 2 process. It is unclear whether exactly 100 iterations were run or up to 100 with early stopping. A 100-iteration OC run may not have converged, so this changes the result.
readings: At most 100 iterations, stop early if relative compliance change < 1e-3
At most 100 iterations, stop early if relative compliance change < 1e-4
At most 100 iterations, stop early if max density change < 0.01

items.entity: OC update parameters (move limit m, damping exponent η)
items.description: Eqs. 9–10 use m and η (m, η > 0) but give no values. In Eq. 10, m multiplies B_e instead of acting as a move limit (ρ ± m), and Eq. 9 has no move-limit clamp. Sec. 2 also calls the method 'gradient descent'. With a fixed 100 iterations, these values change the final design.
readings: Standard OC: move limit m = 0.2 (ρ ± m bounds), η = 0.5, λ found by bisection
Eq. 9 taken literally: no move limit, η = 0.5

items.entity: Void stiffness E_min / density lower bound ρ_min
items.description: Eq. 2 uses modified SIMP with E_min (no value given). Eq. 9 also clamps densities at ρ_min (no value given). Eq. 8's sensitivity leaves out the (E0 − E_min) factor. The text does not settle which scheme was used or with what values.

The starting design of the SIMP run is never stated. The 'full material presence' in Sec. 4.1 refers only to the analysis used to build the stress/strain input fields. The problem is non-convex and capped at 100 iterations, so the starting design affects the result.

items.entity: Thresholding to the binary topology map
items.description: Sec. 2 says 'a thresholding step is applied' and Sec. 4.1 stores 'a binary topology map', but neither gives the threshold rule or value. The text also does not say whether the ground-truth compliance is computed on the binary design or the grey SIMP design.
readings: Volume-preserving threshold (keep the round(f·4096) highest-density elements)
No threshold; compliance computed on the grey SIMP design

items.entity: Young's modulus E0 of the solid
items.description: Sec. 2 defines E0 only as a symbol; no value is given anywhere.
Poisson's ratio is not mentioned anywhere. It changes the element stiffness non-proportionally, so it can alter the optimal layout.

items.entity: 2D elasticity assumption (plane stress vs plane strain)
items.description: Sec. 2 and Sec. 4.1 do not say whether the 2D analysis is plane stress or plane strain. Plane strain behaves like plane stress with a different effective Poisson's ratio, which changes the stiffness non-proportionally.
Sec. 4.1 says only '64×64 square elements'. The element formulation and integration rule are not given.

items.entity: Physical side length and out-of-plane thickness of the square domain
items.description: Sec. 4.1 gives a square domain meshed into 64×64 elements, but no physical side length or thickness. For square Q4 elements under point loads the side length does not change the compliance, and the thickness only scales it. The exception would be a filter radius defined in physical units.

The text mentions no passive regions. It does not say whether solid elements were enforced under the load or at the supports. The 'load discrepancy' metric in Sec. 5 checks for material at the load point, but this does not settle it.
readings: Passive solid element(s) under the loaded node
Passive solid elements at the fixed points/segments
